newsitem.title: USA: H.F.Ahmanson bids for Great Western.
newsitem.headline: H.F.Ahmanson bids for Great Western.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co said Tuesday it had offered to acquire Great Western Financial Corp in a stock swap valued at $6 billion.
Under the offer, Los Angeles-based Ahmanson said it would swap 1.05 of its shares for each Great Western share. The bid values Great Western shares at $42.53 each, Ahmanson said.
Ahmanson, which has made three nominations to Great Western's board, said it expects "immediate and substantial" earnings-per-share accretion from the transaction. It gave no specific figures.
It said the deal would be accounted for as a purchase.
The transaction, which would be tax-free, is subject to approval by regulators and the boards of both companies.
Ahmanson said the transaction would save it more than $400 million in pre-tax costs by 1999.

It said the cost-savings, coupled with planned stock repurchases, would mean a 5.0 percent accretion to its earnings per share in 1997, a 15 percent accretion in 1998, and a 26 percent accretion in 1999.
"Furthermore, the transaction would be accretive to reported earnings per share by the end of the fourth quarter of 1998, and 9.0 percent accretive in 1999," Ahmanson said.
The transaction would create a combined company with about $93 billion in assets, it said.
Ahmanson is the largest U.S. thrift, and Great Western is its biggest rival.

Ahmanson said its nominees to Great Western's board are Lawrence Del Santo, chairman of Vons Cos Inc ; Robert Gelber, former partner of the law firm Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher, and Wolfgang Schoellkopf, former vice chairman and chief financial officer of First Fidelity Bancorp.
Ahmanson shares closed Friday at 40-1/2, while Great Western shares closed at 34-1/2.

Ahmanson said its bid provides Great Western shareholders with an initial premium of 24.2 percent over Great Western's closing market price on Friday, and represents a multiple of 2.7 times Great Western's tangible book value as of December 31, 1996.

Ahmanson said the combined companies would be based in the greater Los Angeles area. The merger is expected to result in a consolidation of approximately 25 percent of the branches in the combined system, it said.
